no-bounds-check? A rotated counted loop has exactly one conditional branch, its latch; the check is a second one. inner-loop finds the latch as the backward conditional branch with the latest head. loop-exit-branches is the stronger reading (target outside the body) for linked images, where displacements are real.

Note gcc 15.2 picks vfmadd132pd where the bead's prose says 231; the 132/213/231 is operand order and the whole family counts.

poll-free? preempt.ss's predicate is over mnemonics and no real ISA spells a poll 'poll', so the mnemonic half can only ever catch our own pseudo-ops. Wired to a sequence recognizer: a scalar integer load from a non-indexed address followed within 3 instructions by a conditional branch, which is the shape of the global suspend word in every runtime PREEMPTION.md cites, and which excludes the loop's own data stream (indexed, and in the float or vector file). Deliberately over-broad, as preempt.ss asks.

MET. 2242 -> 1820 instructions/step, against sbcl-5 at 2015.00 -- a 9.7% margin. chez-4 (1788.41) is now 1.8% ahead rather than 25%.

Three passes, in the order they were found to matter:

MOVE COALESCING (regalloc.ss). A vreg that is a move's destination prefers the
source's register. The source is still ACTIVE at that point -- a move's source
is read at the instruction defining its destination, so linear scan's
'end < start' expiry has not released it -- so this TRANSFERS the register and
drops the source's interval from the active list. The first version shared it
instead and let expiry hand the register back to the free pool while the
destination was still living in it. Two values, one register: no assertion
fires, the answer is just wrong.

DEAD CODE ELIMINATION (dce.ss, new). There was none. Elision proves n-bodies
is 3 and rewrites the USE, leaving the gref that loaded it; lowering names
every intermediate whether or not it survives. Criterion is deliberately crude
-- dead means used as an operand NOWHERE, not 'nowhere after here' -- because
per-point liveness on a CFG is a dataflow question and erring toward 'looks
dead' deletes what a back edge reads next iteration.

CSE (cse.ss, new), block-local, rewriting uses rather than inserting moves.
The hot body computed i+1 three times and i+2 three times, 27 of 53
instructions.

WHAT IT COST TO GET RIGHT: CSE made nbody wrong in the twelfth digit, and the
fault was in finalize, not CSE. resolve-argument-moves recovers a parallel
copy by pattern-matching the register listing, and admitted a constant-pool
load as a copy member. A parallel copy permutes values that exist; a pool load
makes one. Once the three 0.0 accumulators were one value, the entry stub read
xmm0 before anything wrote it. Fixed by drawing the line at the base register:
[rsp+N] is a spill slot and stays in the copy, every other memory source is a
definition and is hoisted ahead of it. Regression test added.

48 suites 0 failures, nbody bit-exact both energies, RISC-V smoke clean.

DONE. convert.ss, plus the backward propagation in repr.ss that makes it a one-site pass.

RESOLVED AT THE DEFINITION, NOT THE EDGE (ledger D31). The bead proposed
converting on edges -- call site for a parameter, predecessor for a phi. That
is three placements with three sets of control-flow reasoning, and it is
unnecessary: repr.ss already pushes requirements BACKWARD along all three edge
kinds, so once its fixpoint settles, a mismatch cannot survive on an edge. It
survives only at a let whose variable joined up to tagged while its
initializer still produces a raw word.

Two thirds of that backward propagation was already there (the call-site
rule). Added the phi-operand rule and the tail-position rule. Without the
first, phi elimination copies a raw word into the merge variable's value
register; without the second, a two-armed procedure returns 0 or 1 in the
value class on half its paths.

WHAT THE BEAD MISSED: the FIXNUM case was not merely unimplemented, it was
SILENTLY WRONG. The boolean join raised, which is visible. The computed-fixnum
join answered tagged with no conversion and left an untagged machine word in
the value class for the collector to scavenge. That is the case that mattered.

NO NEW MACH-OP. Shift-left-3 is a multiply by 8; the OR of imm-tag is an add
because the shifted form's low three bits are clear. mul and add already have
rules on both targets. A dedicated shift op would save one instruction on a
path that appears only where a program mixes representations, and cost two
selectors, two encoders and the tests for both.

STILL OPEN, deliberately: raw-f64 -> tagged. It is a heap box with a GC map,
not a missing instruction, and needs the allocator. repr.ss still raises and
names it. Filed as a follow-up under E7.
